body.objective: Add one fast, read-only Science Forge coordinator command that answers, from the folded authoritative programme state: what is running, what is ready next, what is blocked and why, which streams are about to drain, what certified results just landed, and which cross-stream or Forge requests need action. The existing `s-f streams-view --now T -o file.md` is a useful complete generated view but is too slow and bulky for a frequent coordination loop, requires a file plus follow-up extraction, and does not provide a compact recent-results/action feed.
body.stop_condition: Land a documented command such as `s-f overview --now <T>` (name may differ if consistent with the CLI grammar) that auto-detects the programme and writes a compact human-readable dashboard to stdout in one invocation. It must include: (1) one row per stream with ACTIVE item and lease holder/expiry, ready queue depth in exact work-pull order, blocked count, and the next pullable item; (2) explicit health findings for ACTIVE-without-live-lease, live-lease-without-ACTIVE, READY-but-no-active-worker, ACTIVE-with-no-dependent-or-ready-reserve, expired/ambiguous lease, unresolved cross-stream request, and queue drained; (3) recent terminal results over a caller-specified deterministic window or count, showing item, DONE/OBSTRUCTED/SHORTFALL disposition, evidence basis, reported commit, and one-line next recommendation; (4) open dependency requests and physics-to-Forge requests grouped by state and affected stream; (5) compact global totals and a clearly ordered coordinator action list; (6) `--stream`, `--recent <N>`, `--json`, and `--strict` filters/modes, with the JSON schema versioned and byte-stable for fixed inputs; (7) stdout by default, optional `-o`, and no title mutation; (8) a fast path that folds/parses the programme once and is benchmarked on the current physics corpus, with a target well below the current approximately 20-30 second streams-view latency; and (9) deterministic fixtures covering healthy multi-stream work, drained queue, active-without-reserve, blocked dependency, stale lease, recent exact result, recent obstruction, SHORTFALL, and open Forge request. The command must state that ACTIVE/lease means scheduled work, not proof of a live OS process; an optional separately typed runtime overlay may be added later but must never become authoritative lifecycle evidence.
body.forbid: no lifecycle transition, lease acquisition, queue repair, git write, paper edit, terminal title change, wall-clock fallback, process killing, or scientific inference; no use of embeddings or text similarity to choose priority; no hiding blocked or SHORTFALL work behind aggregate counts; no treating an uncommitted file, OS process, window title, or prose claim as a landed scientific result; no hand ordering that differs from work-pull readiness; no making the full Markdown streams-view slower or less complete; no requiring the coordinator to grep, parse Markdown, or inspect event JSON after running the command.
notes: First consumer is the recurring physics coordinator sweep across black-hole, bridge, classical, nonlinear, observer, and quantum-qme streams.
Desired common invocation: `s-f overview --now "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" --recent 8`; deterministic core still requires the explicit timestamp.

The existing accepted SF7 request covers worker-facing CLI help and work show/list. This request is the cross-stream coordinator surface and should reuse the same folded-state implementation rather than duplicate it.

Recent results should come from authoritative WORK_REPORTED and terminal transition evidence, not raw git-log subject heuristics. A git/runtime overlay, if offered, must be labeled advisory and separate.
